entries.initial_prompt:
Create a polished, precise desktop UI design proposal for Slate, a native vector canvas application. This is a NEW design mockup, not a retouch of the current UI. Reference image 1 is the POSITIVE reference for Slate's quiet thin outline icon family. Reference images 2 and 3 show the CURRENT BAD UI: preserve only the dark canvas and selected teal rectangle context. REPLACE their circular buttons, bulky generic controls, enormous detached popup, duplicated RGB rows, and intrusive inside dimension badges.

Mandatory Slate style: near-black canvas #0e1013; panel #121416; subdued surface #1c2026; subtle hairline border #363c42; offwhite #dde2e8; muted labels #878e96; restrained teal #2dd4bf for active controls; pale blue #6fb7ff only for geometry selection and dimensional witness lines. Clean system sans serif, crisp text, no branding or glossy marketing treatment. Quiet outline icons have consistent 1.5-unit strokes, rounded caps and joins, open interiors, a single clear metaphor. Buttons are softly SQUARED SUPERELLIPSES (squircles, exponent 2.5), matching Slate's primary dock: never circular or capsule button containers. The circular thumb on a slider and the actual ellipse icon are acceptable; the tool button silhouette must be squircle. Three approximately 32 board-unit buttons, fill, stroke, corners, have about 7 units between them. Subtle active teal background, restrained borders, no colorful oversized tiles.

Critical spatial rule: the selection, its dimension stringers, three-button strip, and open editor are ONE host-relative assembly in board space. The editor grows UP and AWAY from the shape, anchored immediately above the active button with a small consistent gap; no floating inspector at a screen corner. The entire assembly including typography, padding, icons, strokes and gaps scales with camera zoom. Never viewport-clamp or freeze an editor in screen coordinates. Keep all buttons and panels clear of the selected shape.

Dimensions are precise architectural stringers entirely OUTSIDE the rectangle: width BELOW and height to the RIGHT, thin witness lines with small diagonal end ticks, centered understated numeric labels '180 u' and '120 u', small canvas-colored knockout behind text only. No heavy black badges, no unnecessary decimals, no dimensions in the property editor. Both witness lines and labels stay clear of the object.

Make a landscape presentation image with TWO large, clean mockups side by side, same scale and aligned shape baselines: left Fill editor open, right Corners editor open. Both show the same teal rectangle with thin selected blue outline, each with its own three-squircle strip directly above. Each example is a plausible pixel-sharp app screen with generous but intentional breathing room. Tiny calm title at top, tiny 'Fill' and 'Corners' captions above the two examples; no walls of explanatory text, no unrelated app sidebars. Fill editor uses ONE RGB row, a desktop eyedropper icon, compact saturation/value color field, slim hue rail, opacity control closest to the toolbar. Eyedropper's short tooltip if shown says 'Sample desktop'. Corners editor contains Fillet / Chamfer binary control, Units / % binary control, slender radius slider and numeric value. Show 50% fillet and a visibly but moderately rounded rectangle on the right. 100% means radius half the shorter side: circle for a square, diamond for square chamfer. No generic egui widgets, no U8 label, no giant Apply/Cancel bars. Avoid decorative shadows, extra chrome, extraneous controls. Design must be realistic to implement with native vector primitives, not fantasy UI.

Title 'A · Focused stack'. RECOMMENDED DIRECTION. The compact editor is a single narrow, beautifully composed panel centered above its active squircle. Fill panel is about 250 logical units wide, with a compact 220x92 color field near the top, hue rail underneath, a tidy R 45 G 212 B 191 row with an eyedropper squircle, and a thin opacity slider with '100%' on its right at the very bottom. Keep about 10 units between editor and icon strip, and 16 between icon strip and rectangle. Corners panel is matching width but shorter; equal-size Fillet/Chamfer choices with little geometric corner glyphs at top, a subtle Units/% choice and value '50%' below, then a slender slider. Rectangle and controls carefully balanced, quiet, direct and minimal. A faint short central connector between active squircle and panel can clarify ownership without adding heavy brackets.
entries.refinement_prompt: Refine this Slate UI mockup while preserving the overall composition and its 'A' option name. This is a precision UI edit, not a redesign. In the Corners panel, the 'Percent' mode must be SELECTED (subtle teal fill and teal outline) and the 'Units' mode must be UNSELECTED dark. Keep the numeric radius 50%. Current reference has the wrong selected unit. Remove the duplicate internal Fill and Corners headings while retaining small example captions outside the panels, reclaim their empty header space so panels are shorter. Shorten the cartoon speech-bubble pointer below Corners to a tiny 5-unit caret, matching the tiny fill pointer. Keep opacity at the bottom of the Fill editor nearest the icon strip. Retain the same clearly distinct fill bucket, outline circle stroke and rounded-corner icon glyphs inside softly squared squircle buttons. Use FLAT solid fills for the teal geometry and dark panel surfaces, no gradients except inside the color picker, no glow, no simulated material texture. Preserve restrained thin offwhite outline icons and the Slate near-black palette. Keep all dimension stringers outside the shapes. Keep crisp legible typography. Refined, quiet, plausible native app UI.
entries.cleanup_prompt: Make only these small corrections to this existing Slate concept sheet. Preserve everything else, including exact layout, text, color picker, RGB, sliders, dimensions, squircle buttons and title. 1. REMOVE ALL triangular speech-bubble pointers from the bottom edges of both editor panels. Make both panel bottom edges plain straight horizontal with their existing softened outer corners. 2. In the right Corners panel, give Fillet the same subtle teal selected fill and teal outline as the selected Percent button; Chamfer stays dark unselected. 3. Restore a thin pale-blue selection outline around each teal rectangle. Do not add or remove any controls or change any other active states. Pixel-sharp UI.

In the RIGHT example's three squircle tool buttons, deactivate the LEFT paint-bucket button to a dark fill with gray outline; activate the RIGHT corner-outline button with the existing subtle teal selected treatment. Middle Stroke button stays dark. This is the Corners example so Corners must be active, not Fill. Keep the LEFT example's Fill button active.
